text:
Maria Lopez: Heads-up — I'll be handing off the sfo2 GPU cluster (sfo2-gpu-prod) to the on-call rotation tomorrow 2026-03-19 09:00 PT. Quick summary: cluster is bootstrapped, kubelet + NV drivers installed, autoscaler policy set, but we still need to validate networking MTU and NFS mounts. Runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/sfo2-provisioning (please read before the handoff).

Jake Kim: ack, I'll join the 09:00 handoff. Can you paste the immediate contact/escalation path?

Maria Lopez: Sure — pager routing in order: 1) primary oncall (rotation @oncall) pager -> 2) senior-sre (after 12m if no ack) -> 3) infra-eng lead (after 30m). Pager service is `pagerduty:RDW-SFO2-GPU`. Slack escalation channel is #sfo2-oncall-escalations.

Priya Rao: added the runbook to my bookmarks. For MTU failures we recently saw, the quick triage is: check VPC MTU, then check host MTU and `calico` config. If pods can't reach image registry it's usually an MTU/fragmentation issue.

Thomas Ng: I've added a small validation checklist to the runbook but copying key checks here: 
- ensure node allocatable shows GPUs (`kubectl get nodes -o=custom-columns=NODE:.metadata.name,GPUS:.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu`)
- confirm nv_driver pods running: `kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l app=nvidia-driver`
- run a quick GPU pod: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: cuda-smoke
spec:
  containers:
  - name: cuda
    image: nvidia/cuda:11.7-runtime-ubuntu20.04
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1
    command: ["/bin/sh","-c","nvidia-smi && sleep 5"]
  restartPolicy: Never
```
- check autoscaler scale-up with a synthetic job (`kubectl run gpu-test --image=alpine --command -- sleep 60` -> this should trigger pending pods that cause scale up)

Maria Lopez: Networking specifics: internal load balancer for model-serving is using TCP idle timeout 600s; we experienced a connection drop if MTU != 1500. NFS mount point is on the storage nodes at `/mnt/model-store` — double-check permissions and that the export is mounted with `noatime`.

Jake Kim: What about cost guardrails for the region? We need a hard cap so accidental burst doesn't blow the budget.

Maria Lopez: Good catch — billing tags applied: `env:prod`, `cluster:sfo2-gpu`, `team:platform`. We also set a soft quota alert at 60% of committed GPU hours and a hard quota that prevents new node creation past 95% (via the provisioning controller). Alerts -> Ops channel + Pager after threshold.

Priya Rao: Training note: I'll run a 30-min walkthrough 08:30-09:00 PT tomorrow covering runbook, common triage commands, and escalation samples. I'll record it and drop the link.

Thomas Ng: Commands (copyable) for quick triage: 
```
# list GPU nodes
kubectl get nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=gpu-pool -o wide

# show gpu allocatable
kubectl get nodes -o=custom-columns=NODE:.metadata.name,GPUS:.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu

# check kubelet logs for OOM or driver errors
gcloud compute ssh $NODE --zone $ZONE --command "sudo journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager | tail -n 200"

# check dmesg for GPU attach failures
gcloud compute ssh $NODE --zone $ZONE --command "dmesg | grep -i nvidia || true"
```

Maria Lopez: A few gotchas we've seen — if the autoscaler can't allocate a GPU SKU because Zonal capacity is low, the controller will retry and you'll see pending pods with `PodFitsResources` and `FailedScheduling` events. In that case: 
- check GCP quota for GPU in the zone `gcloud compute regions describe us-west2 --format=json | jq .quotas`
- if quota is fine, check cloud provider capacity (sometimes region is temporarily constrained) and switch routing policy to fallback pool (see runbook section 4.3).

Jake Kim: For the handoff itself, what's expected of the oncaller during the first 2 hours?

Maria Lopez: During initial 2 hours: monitor dashboards (Console -> cluster -> nodes, latency SLI), watch for scaledown flapping, ensure no model-serving 5xx spike. If there's an incident, follow the Incident -> Triage -> Escalate path in the runbook. If nothing happens, mark the handoff acceptance post in #eng-oncall with `handoff accepted` and the checklist completed (I added a template in the runbook).

oncall-bot: Reminder: scheduled handoff for sfo2-gpu-prod at 2026-03-19T16:00:00Z (09:00 PT). A training session is set for 2026-03-19T15:30:00Z (08:30 PT).

Priya Rao: will post the recording and the short cheat sheet (one-pager) after the session. Also, if someone wants a quick shadow session earlier DM me.

Thomas Ng: pinging @infra-bot for verifying the GCP quota snapshot and attaching output to the runbook.

infra-bot: Quota snapshot attached in runbook: `gcp-quota-sfo2-1829991234.json` — GPUs: requested 120, limit 200, available 80.

Jake Kim: all good from me. thanks Maria, see you at 08:30 for the training. :thumbsup:

Maria Lopez: thanks team — I'll update the runbook with the final checklist and post the handoff message in #eng-oncall once I confirm the NFS mount validation.
